title: The Follies Bergere in Chicago with Sally Rand
summary: In Chicago in 1933 Zutty played the Selby act in the Follies Bergere floor show, sitting in the band beside George Wettling, with Sally Rand and Joe E. Lewis in the show.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well what did you go back to Chicago for then?

Well I went back with Arlene and Norman Selby. We played in the Follies Bergere. That's when Sally Rand made a big hit at the Fair. See, because I played with Irving Rothstein, Rothstien, Rothchild or somebody. His band was playing the show. You see, a big show. They had Joe E. Lewis was in the show. That's when, just right after he got in all that trouble when he got beat up that time. You see, and Sally Rand was in the show.
You weren't in orchestra, you were playing an act were you?
I'd sit in to play the act. George Wettling was the drummer with the band.
You got into the band because it was a floor show you know?
Oh, of course. I was thinking of the theater, yes.

It was a floor show. And it looked like Sally Rand wasn't wearing nothing then. Because she had to walk right by me, see? And I'm afraid if I look up and see all them cats will be looking at me. (LAUGHTER). Because they didn't want me to see that at all. And they had a part of the show where they had a girl standing way up high in the show see? And boy when she'd take her hands back there was nothing there, see. And I never did miss that. (LAUGHTER).
Man, I digged that boy and cats was kind of half sulking with me. (LAUGHTER). They didn't want me to even look at her.
